title: Life Cycle of a Butterfly: Four Acts
description: Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly — the four acts of metamorphosis, and what actually happens inside the chrysalis (it is not sleeping).

body.heading: One animal, four bodies
paragraphs: A butterfly does not grow the way you do, getting a bit bigger each year. It changes its whole body, four separate times — a complete transformation called metamorphosis. It is as if a fish turned into a bird halfway through its life. Here are the four acts.

body.heading: Act 1 and 2: egg and caterpillar
paragraphs: Act 1 — Egg. A mother butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf — usually the exact leaf her babies will love to eat. In a few days, out chew the tiniest caterpillars.
Act 2 — Caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is eating. It munches and grows, and munches and grows, shedding its too-tight skin four or five times, like outgrowing four coats in a month.

body.heading: Act 3: the chrysalis
paragraphs: Act 3 — Chrysalis. When it is fully grown, the caterpillar hangs upside down and builds a quiet case around itself called a chrysalis. It looks like it is sleeping. It is not.

Inside, its body comes apart and rebuilds into a completely different animal — wings, long legs, curly tongue and all. This is the most astonishing construction job in nature, done without hands, in about two weeks.

body.heading: Act 4: butterfly
paragraphs: Act 4 — Butterfly. The case splits, and out climbs a butterfly with wet, crumpled wings. It pumps them full, lets them dry in the sun, and flies away to sip flower nectar and lay eggs of its own — starting the whole four-act play again.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. The caterpillar sheds its skin when it outgrows it. What do YOU outgrow — and what do you do with the things you outgrow?
2. If you could ask the chrysalis one question, what would it be?

takeaway: A butterfly lives four lives — egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly — and the quiet chrysalis is where its body is taken apart and rebuilt.
